subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: An isotope pair
hotspots.description: Two carbon atoms: carbon-12 and carbon-14. Same red protons, different gray neutron counts — an isotope pair.
hotspots.positionHint: The two atom nuclei side by side.
hotspots.function: Shows two isotopes of the same element.

hotspots.label: The identical protons
hotspots.description: Both atoms have the same number of red protons — 6 each. This is what makes them BOTH carbon.
hotspots.positionHint: The red proton spheres in both nuclei.
hotspots.function: Shows the proton count that stays the same.

hotspots.label: The differing neutrons
hotspots.description: Carbon-12 has 6 gray neutrons; carbon-14 has 8. The extra neutrons make carbon-14 heavier — and radioactive, which is what lets it date ancient bones.
hotspots.positionHint: The gray neutron spheres, differing between the two nuclei.
hotspots.function: Shows the neutron count that varies between isotopes.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. Two atom nuclei float side by side with faint electron clouds, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Protons: soft red spheres; neutrons: soft gray spheres; electron clouds: faint translucent warm-white shells. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / coral / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Protons: soft muted red, roughness ~0.4. Neutrons: soft muted gray, roughness ~0.4. Electron clouds: translucent warm-white shells, alpha ~0.1. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a carbon-12 / carbon-14 isotope pair, built to be read as 'same element, different weight — the neutrons differ.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: two carbon atom nuclei side by side (spacing ~1.6), each a compact bundle with faint translucent electron-cloud shells: LEFT carbon-12 — 6 soft red proton spheres + 6 soft gray neutron spheres (radius ~0.2 each); RIGHT carbon-14 — 6 soft red proton spheres + 8 soft gray neutron spheres. The two extra neutrons on the right are slightly visually separated so they read as 'extra.'

2) PARTICLE COUNT (toggleable layer): the protons on both atoms highlight briefly one by one (6 each), then the neutrons highlight one by one (6 vs 8) — making the identical-count and differing-count obvious. App renders small running tallies.

3) USES (toggleable layer): small floating icons appear beside carbon-14 (app-rendered glyphs) — a bone (dating), a medical cross (medicine), and a plant/building (nuclear power) — linking the extra neutrons to real uses.

Camera: framed so both nuclei and their clouds fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: Carbon12_Nucleus, Carbon14_Nucleus, Protons_06, Neutrons_C12, Neutrons_C14, ExtraNeutrons_02, Cloud_C12, Cloud_C14, UseIcons. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
